title: Chapter 95 — AI Foundations for Appliance Sales
intro: What AI is, what it is not, and the mental model for using it effectively on the sales floor.

sections.title: What AI Actually Is
sections.content:
AI in the context of appliance sales is a tool that processes language, data, and patterns faster than you can. It can draft emails, compare products, research brands, summarize customer interactions, and simulate practice conversations.

What it is not: a replacement for your judgment, your relationships, or your floor instincts. It cannot read the customer's body language. It cannot feel the energy shift when you mention a price. It cannot tell that the wife loves the range but the husband is nervous about the budget.

The mental model: AI is your research assistant and your practice partner. It handles the time-consuming, information-heavy tasks so you can focus on the human-heavy tasks — rapport, trust, closing, and service.

sections.title: The AI-Enhanced Workflow
sections.content:
Before the customer arrives: use AI to research a brand you are unfamiliar with. Get the selling angles, competitive positioning, and common objections in minutes instead of hours.

During the sale: use AI for real-time product comparisons, competitive cross-references, and spec lookups. The customer asks 'what is the difference between these two dishwashers?' and you have a detailed comparison in 30 seconds.

After the sale: use AI to draft the follow-up email, the quote summary, and the referral ask. Edit for your voice and send.

Between customers: use AI to analyze your pipeline, identify follow-up priorities, and practice objection handling through roleplay scenarios.

sections.title: The Verification Habit
sections.content:
The single most important AI habit: verify everything before it reaches the customer. AI generates plausible-sounding information that may be wrong. A model number that is close but not exact. A spec that was true last year but changed. A price from a discontinued promotion.

Verify model numbers against the PIM or manufacturer spec sheet. Verify pricing against your current system. Verify delivery dates against your actual availability. The five-minute verification is non-negotiable.
